args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1, the service failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying, and check why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions and is healthy again. I opened a SEV2 incident for it, which paged on-call.

1. **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
2. **Rollback:** I chose v2.3.0 because it's the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
3. **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2) is open. It says what happened, what I did and what's left to follow up.

v2.3.1 also failed in staging (as v2.3.1-rc), so a release that was already failing there was still pushed to production. The incident asks for a root-cause check on v2.3.1 before anyone redeploys it, and a look at why it got promoted.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
